background: Societe Generale is one of France's three largest banks, a universal bank with French retail networks, a large derivatives-driven investment bank, the Ayvens car-leasing business and banking subsidiaries in Africa and Central Europe.
synthesis: Societe Generale is rated A+ on average across all three main agencies, the weakest of them at A, the outlooks split one negative, one positive and one stable, after a two-notch upgrade by one of the three on 12 May 2026. The balance sheet is on the weak side of EU and Nordic banks: CET1 of 13.2%, leverage of 4.3% and NSFR of 115% are all in the bottom quarter and LCR of 146% is below the peer median. None of the ratios has moved materially over the past four periods (figures to 30 Jun 2026). The only flagged item, on 22 Sep 2026, is a raised profitability target, which the market welcomed.
